subject.title: feat(msteams): add native plugin interactivity parity

question: Should this Teams parity work continue as a Teams-specific plugin runtime/API surface, or should it be narrowed onto current main's generic interactive and channel-route contracts before merge?
rationale: The branch adds public plugin runtime/API and security-sensitive Teams operations while current main has newer generic channel-route and registry-owned interactive contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term API shape.

options.title: Rebase and narrow onto current contracts
options.body: Preserve the Teams parity goal, but rebuild it on current main's generic channel-route, interactive registry, and SQLite state seams before another merge review.

options.title: Accept a Teams-specific runtime surface
options.body: Keep runtime.channel.msteams as a deliberate public escape hatch, but require maintainer API approval, docs/baseline alignment, upgrade tests, and live tenant proof.

options.title: Pause behind the lane-oriented PR
options.body: Defer this branch until the broader lane-oriented channel interface direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59986 is resolved.

recommendation.title: Rebase and narrow onto current contracts
recommendation.body: Preserve the Teams parity goal, but rebuild it on current main's generic channel-route, interactive registry, and SQLite state seams before another merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signals for channel-route APIs, Teams state storage, and plugin SDK direction point to steipete.
